items.syntax: WITH name AS (SELECT …) SELECT … FROM name
items.explanation: Makes multi-step logic readable top to bottom.
items.example: WITH big AS (SELECT order_id, freight FROM orders WHERE freight > 100) SELECT COUNT(*) AS big_orders FROM big;
items.expected: One row: number of orders with freight over 100.

items.syntax: WITH a AS (…), b AS (SELECT … FROM a) SELECT …
items.explanation: Later CTEs can read earlier ones.
items.example: WITH rev AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(freight) AS f FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id), avg_rev AS (SELECT AVG(f) AS a FROM rev) SELECT r.customer_id, r.f FROM rev r, avg_rev WHERE r.f > avg_rev.a ORDER BY r.f DESC;
items.expected: Customers whose total freight exceeds the average.

items.syntax: WITH totals AS (… GROUP BY k) SELECT … FROM t JOIN totals USING (k)
items.explanation: Aggregate before joining to avoid fan-out.
items.example: WITH n AS (SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT c.category_name, n.products FROM categories c JOIN n USING (category_id) ORDER BY n.products DESC;

items.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE s(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM s WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM s
items.explanation: Anchor plus recursive step; stops when the step returns nothing.
items.example: WITH RECURSIVE s(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM s WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM s;

items.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (anchor UNION ALL SELECT … JOIN t ON …)
items.explanation: Follows parent/child links to any depth.
items.example: WITH RECURSIVE org AS (SELECT employee_id, first_name, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE reports_to IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, org.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN org ON e.reports_to = org.employee_id) SELECT * FROM org ORDER BY level;
items.expected: Every employee with their org-chart level.

items.explanation: PostgreSQL 12+ inlines single-use CTEs; MATERIALIZED forces one evaluation, NOT MATERIALIZED forces inlining.
items.example: WITH x AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE freight > 50) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM x;
items.expected: One row: count of orders with freight over 50.

items.operation: Write and read in one statement
items.syntax: WITH d AS (DELETE … RETURNING *) SELECT … FROM d
items.explanation: PostgreSQL-specific: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE inside WITH, consumed by the outer query.
items.example: WITH d AS (DELETE FROM order_details WHERE quantity < 5 RETURNING order_id, quantity) SELECT COUNT(*) AS deleted_lines, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM d;
items.expected: One row: deleted line count and units (rolled back).
